_audit_note: Evidence classification: [PE]=Physically Established, [SP]=Standard/Procedure Dependent, [FA]=Facility/ATE Dependent, [SA]=Synthetic Assumption, [UA]=Unknown/Requires Authoritative Documentation

THERMAL_BURN_IN._note: Canonical burn-in: DUT biased at elevated temperature for extended time. Static operating conditions. Primary test for DIGITAL_IC reliability screening.
THERMAL_BURN_IN.standard_reference: [SP] MIL-STD-883 Method 1015 (Burn-In); ESCC 9000 Level S/B; NASA EEE-INST-002 Sec 4.
THERMAL_BURN_IN._checkpoint_note: [SP] Checkpoint intervals are PS #26170 mandated (0h, 24h, 96h, 168h). Duration and temperature are device/class specific [UA].

temperature_c.evidence: [SP] MIL-STD-883 M1015 specifies 125°C as standard; actual limit device-specific [UA]

bias_voltage.evidence: [SP] Applied at rated VCC; derating per NASA EEE-INST-002 for space screening

duration_hours.evidence: [SP] 168h is a common space-grade duration; mission-specific [UA]

MEMS_THERMAL_STRESS._note: MEMS sensors are subjected to controlled thermal stress to trigger viscoelastic stress relaxation and accelerate ZRO drift stabilization. Test sequence and conditions differ from IC burn-in [SP].
MEMS_THERMAL_STRESS.standard_reference: [SP] General aerospace inertial sensor qualification practice; device-specific spec [UA]. ESCC 9000 storage/operational temperature. Not standardized identically to MIL-STD-883 IC burn-in [UA].
MEMS_THERMAL_STRESS._checkpoint_note: [SA] Applied same PS-compatible checkpoint structure for dataset consistency. Actual MEMS screening duration is facility-dependent [UA].

temperature_c.evidence: [PE/SA] Lower than IC burn-in; MEMS mechanical reliability requires avoiding stiction at high T. Exact value facility-dependent [UA]

humidity_pct.evidence: [SP] Dry environment required; moisture causes MEMS stiction

duration_hours.evidence: [SA] Applied for cross-lot comparability; actual duration [UA]

IMAGE_SENSOR_DARK_CURRENT_TEST.display_name: CMOS Image Sensor Dark Current & Non-Uniformity Characterization
IMAGE_SENSOR_DARK_CURRENT_TEST._note: Image sensors measured in dark conditions at elevated temperature to accelerate and characterize dark current. Not the same as IC burn-in biasing [SP].
IMAGE_SENSOR_DARK_CURRENT_TEST.standard_reference: [SP] EMVA 1288 standard for imager characterization; GSFC-STD-7000 for space imaging systems. Device-specific qualification [UA].
IMAGE_SENSOR_DARK_CURRENT_TEST._checkpoint_note: [SA] Applied for cross-lot comparability. Actual dark current test is typically shorter; long-exposure test for trap identification [UA].

temperature_c.evidence: [PE] Dark current doubles approximately every 8-10°C; 60°C represents accelerated but non-destructive condition

integration_time_ms.evidence: [SA] Selected for measurable dark signal accumulation; device-specific [UA]

INITIAL_ELECTRICAL_SCREENING._note: Single-point baseline measurement taken at ambient before stress. Not a time-series test itself, but provides the t=0h anchor for all subsequent drift calculations.
INITIAL_ELECTRICAL_SCREENING.standard_reference: [SP] ESCC 9000 / MIL-STD-883 Method 5004. Required before any burn-in or stress test.

THERMO_VACUUM._note: Simulates on-orbit thermal vacuum environment. Used for system-level and some component-level space qualification. Not identical to component burn-in [SP].
THERMO_VACUUM.standard_reference: [SP] ISRO/IISU TVAC specification; general aerospace environmental test [SP ECSS-E-ST-10-03].

temperature_c.evidence: [SP] Hot case orbit simulation; cold case typically -30 to -40°C [UA mission-specific]
